source.title: Interpreting Attention Layer Outputs with Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Connor Kissane; Robert Krzyzanowski; J. Bloom; Arthur Conmy; Neel Nanda

record.tranche_reason: The study applies sparse autoencoders to attention outputs in language models and reports results on sparse, interpretable feature recovery, extending the superposition-related question to a new model setting. It does not reproduce the toy-model experiments or test their geometry.
record.gate_note: The study reports SAE sparsity, reconstruction fidelity, and human-rated interpretability for language-model attention outputs; these bear on V4's claim that an SAE can recover sparse features. It does not test feature overlap or near-orthogonality, sparsity- or importance-dependent geometry, capacity pressure as the cause of polysemanticity, or whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units. Other head-ablation, induction, and IOI results address different behaviors and are not rows for these claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study trains SAEs on attention-layer outputs (z_cat) of GPT-2 Small, GELU-2L and Gemma-2B, a site not covered by the original. It reports sparsity, loss recovered and human-rated interpretability of the recovered features, which bears on V4's claim that a dictionary can recover sparse features in real LMs. It does not touch the toy-model geometry (V1) or the cause of polysemanticity (V2/V3). It also does not test whether features are complete, stable or canonical units (V5), or whether they are 1-D (V6).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that attention-output SAEs give sparse, reasonably faithful, mostly interpretable decompositions in models up to 2B parameters. They pitch the main contribution as a useful research tool (head roles, long- vs short-prefix induction heads, the IOI positional signal). They estimate at least ~90% of GPT-2 Small heads are polysemantic, and caution that reconstructions are imperfect and may give an incomplete picture.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains sparse autoencoders on concatenated attention-head outputs in trained transformers, rather than testing the toy-model interventions and geometric transitions of the original superposition study.

fits_no_version.finding: In GPT-2 Small, only 14/144 attention heads are plausibly monosemantic, so at least ~90% are polysemantic (Sec 4.1.1, Table 3). Head 10.2's two roles are confirmed by ablation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attention heads (not only neurons) are widely polysemantic in trained LMs.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE features are highly specific at high activations but polysemantic at low activation ranges. Authors attribute this partly to an undersized dictionary and to superposition (App. E.2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dictionary features are monosemantic only above an activation threshold.

record.problems: Interpretability ratings are based on small random samples of 30 live features per layer and subjective author judgment; the authors note these judgments may be flawed. SAEs have imperfect reconstruction, and the authors state that they may provide an incomplete picture. The study focuses mostly on GPT-2 Small, with only limited larger-model coverage.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on the tested V4 recovery claim were left out. The study's head polysemanticity, induction, and IOI results measure other behaviors rather than any of the untested claim versions.

untested.parts: All of it: there is no toy model, no sparsity-dependent phase transition and no feature geometry.
Whether capacity competition causes polysemanticity. The ~90% polysemantic-heads estimate concerns attention heads, and the study does not probe its cause.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
Distribution of features across many MLP neurons. The paper only qualitatively shows some features spread across several attention heads (App. G).
Completeness, stability across seeds or widths, and canonicity. The authors note an undersized dictionary and features that are polysemantic at low activations, but they do not test these properties.
Whether features are intrinsically 1-D. Linearity is assumed by the SAE architecture.

missing.what: IOI splice-in evaluation: SAEs for layers 1-6 preserve logit difference, while layers 0 and 7-11 show notable reconstruction error or high KL.
Automated induction-feature family: 586 candidates, 450 pass the behavioural test vs 3/500 controls, about 5% of non-dead features.
A 'Which'-question feature is computed jointly by 3 heads (>10% variance each), qualitative evidence of features spread across components.

record.verdict_notes: The interpretability ratings come from 30 features per layer, rated by two authors, so the CIs are wide. Gemma-2B used a different loss and training setup and has the highest L0 (90). The L0 values reflect targeted hyperparameters, so they are not evidence for V4 by themselves. Verdicts rest on the % interpretable and % CE-recovered rows.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, more sparse features than dimensions, overlapping nearly orthogonal geometry, and sparsity-dependent transitions.
Whether neuron polysemanticity is caused by capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for other reasons or are evidence for superposition; the reported polysemanticity analysis concerns attention heads.
The study tests SAE recovery of sparse features in language models, but not whether features are distributed across many neurons.
It does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of the model's representation.
SAE features are defined as linear directions in the method, but the study does not test whether the model's underlying features are intrinsically one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

relationships.condition: GPT-2 Small layers 0-6, 9 and 10, and GELU-2L layer 1
relationships.reason: Most sampled live features were rated interpretable (77-97%) and loss recovered was 78-99% (r05,r06,r08,r09,r11,r12,r14,r15,r17,r18,r20,r21,r23,r24,r32,r33,r35,r36,r40,r42,r43). The appendix F induction family (450/586 features pass vs 3/500 controls) corroborates this from the text.
relationships.display_finding: 77–97% of sampled live features were rated interpretable, with 78–99% of loss recovered. An induction feature family passed for 450 of 586 features against 3 of 500 controls.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: GPT-2 Small layers 0-6, 9 and 10, and GELU-2L layer 1
source_check.reason: The listed per-layer rows show 77–97% interpretable sampled live features and 78–99% loss recovered. Appendix F independently reports 450/586 induction candidates passing its behavioral heuristic versus 3/500 controls.

relationships.condition: GPT-2 Small layers 7, 8 and 11, and Gemma-2B layer 6
relationships.reason: Interpretable fractions are lower (60-70%, with CIs reaching ~41-44%) and loss recovered is 75-76% (r02,r03,r26,r27,r29,r30,r38,r39). The text also says layer 0 and 7-11 SAEs show noticeable reconstruction error on IOI (App. K, unrowed).
relationships.display_finding: Interpretable fractions were lower at 60–70%, with confidence intervals reaching about 41–44%, and loss recovered was 75–76%. The paper also reports noticeable reconstruction error on IOI for the layer 0 and 7–11 SAEs.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: GPT-2 Small layers 7, 8 and 11, and Gemma-2B layer 6
source_check.reason: Lower interpretability fractions support a layer/model qualification, but the supplied rationale misstates fidelity: Table 1 gives GPT-2 layers 7, 8 and 11 loss recovered of 83%, 76% and 89%, respectively, and Gemma layer 6 gives 75%. Interpretability is 70%, 60%, 63% and 66%, respectively. Appendix K additionally reports IOI reconstruction limitations.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Section 3 directly evaluates whether SAEs recover sparse, interpretable attention-output features; the study also uses these features for subsequent circuit analysis.

tranche.reason: Attention-head outputs provide a new representation site, with measured sparsity, reconstruction fidelity and feature interpretability bearing on V4.

source_check.notes: Interpretability ratings use 30 sampled live features per SAE and subjective author judgments; confidence intervals overlap. Appendix C cautions that zero-ablation-normalized fidelity is difficult to compare across representation sites.
